title: The Nation That Walked Out of Russia

sentences.text: In 1771, an entire nation tried to walk out of Russia.
The Kalmyks: Buddhist herders on the lower Volga.
They answered to Catherine the Great.
Her empire curbed their khan, seized their pastures, drafted their horsemen.
So in January, Ubashi Khan led some 170,000 people east.
But the Volga never froze, stranding the clans on its west bank.
The rest marched for months, raided and starving.
Tens of thousands never reached China.
The stranded clans are still there: Kalmykia, Europe's only Buddhist republic.
